primitives.name: Bayesian Hierarchical Fielding Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: We combine spatial modeling with a hierarchical Bayesian structure in order to evaluate the performance of individual fielders while sharing information between fielders at each position.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'θ_i': "Fielder i's latent skill parameter (dimensionless)", 'y_{ij}': 'Observed outcome for fielder i on play j (binary: 0/1)', 'x_{ij}': 'Spatial coordinates of batted ball j fielded by i (feet)'}
primitives.assumptions: Players' fielding abilities are modeled as draws from a shared distribution; spatial outcomes follow a Gaussian process.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When spatial resolution is insufficient or when sample size per fielder is too low.

layer2.mapping: The hierarchical structure maps to GSI’s Bayesian inference engine, where θ_i represents posterior belief over fielder skill given observed BIPs.
layer2.telemetry: Runs saved or cost per 1000 balls-in-play

primitives.name: Spatial Batted Ball Density
primitives.verbatim_quote: Specific unsuccessful fielding plays can be deemed to be an "error" by the official scorer at each game.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'f(x,y)': 'Density function of batted balls at location (x,y) (balls per sq ft)', 'BIP': 'Ball-in-play events (count)'}
primitives.assumptions: Batted ball trajectories form a smooth spatial distribution across the field.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At extreme field positions or in sparse data regimes.

layer2.mapping: Density kernel informs GSE’s spatial reasoning module by identifying high-probability zones for fielding.
layer2.telemetry: Contour plots of f(x,y) indicating optimal fielder positioning

primitives.name: Fielding Outcome Probability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Each ball-in-play is either successfully fielded by a defensive player, leading to an out (or multiple outs) on the play, or the ball-in-play is not successfully fielded, resulting in a hit.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p(success | x,y,θ_i)': 'Probability of successful fielding at (x,y) by fielder i (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Outcome depends on fielder skill θ_i and ball location (x,y); binary classification of success/failure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When fielder lacks sufficient data or when ball trajectory is anomalous.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE’s probabilistic state transition model, where p(success) defines action outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Expected value of runs saved per BIP

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper lies in modeling fielding as a spatially distributed stochastic process governed by a Bayesian hierarchical framework. Each fielder's skill is treated as a latent variable drawn from a common distribution, allowing for partial pooling of information across similar positions. This enables robust estimation even with limited per-player data. The spatial component arises from treating batted ball locations as continuous variables, modeled via Gaussian processes. The key innovation is combining this spatial inference with hierarchical priors to produce a scalable, generalizable measure of fielding ability. Failure modes include poor spatial resolution, insufficient BIP counts, or misalignment between model assumptions and actual field dynamics. Dualities emerge in how error assignment versus probabilistic inference reconcile with subjective scoring practices. The model avoids traditional error-based metrics by focusing on likelihood of successful fielding rather than post-hoc categorization.
